title: Catholics under pressure today
hook: in some countries Christians practice their faith at real risk

segments.voice: Yesterday, the underground church: a Liturgy at a kitchen table, until it could be sung in daylight. Your line was the underground church. Whose quiet faithfulness did you notice? Day nine hundred forty-four.

Open an old calendar of martyrs and the scenes come easily: arenas, emperors, ancient Rome. Then open the news. In Nicaragua, a Catholic bishop, Rolando Álvarez, is sentenced to prison and later sent out of the country. In Nigeria, a parish in the town of Owo is attacked during Mass on Pentecost Sunday. In other places, believers meet quietly, because meeting openly could cost them a job, their freedom, or more. Yesterday's underground church is a story with an ending. Today's stories are still going on.
screen: `AN OLD CALENDAR OF MARTYRS.` → `A BISHOP IN PRISON, THEN EXILE.` → `A PARISH ATTACKED AT MASS.`

segments.voice: Start with the word the Church uses for those killed for the faith: martyr. The Church keeps their names, and it is still adding to them. The Acts of the Apostles tells of one of the earliest: Stephen, one of seven men the community chose to serve at its tables, stoned for what he preached. As the stones fall, he prays for the men throwing them, asking the Lord not to hold this sin against them. Second, the Gospel never promised otherwise. In the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims, Jesus says: "Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." Pressure isn't treated as a sign that something went wrong. It's named ahead of time. Third, remembering. The letter to the Hebrews asks its readers to remember prisoners as if they were in chains alongside them, and to remember those who suffer as people living in the same kind of body. That is one reason Catholics in a quiet suburb pray for a parish in Nigeria or a bishop far from home: in that letter's picture, they are not strangers in a headline. Fourth, what pressure looks like now. Sometimes it is violence. Often, those who track it say, it is quieter: laws that close schools and charities, a job lost after a baptism, a priest followed by police, a church that can never get a building permit. And it isn't only Christians. Believers of other faiths face it too, in other places, and the Second Vatican Council taught that religious freedom belongs to every person. Some parishes light their buildings red on a chosen day, red for the martyrs. Others read names aloud at Mass. The point is the same as the old calendars: the names are said, so they are not forgotten.
screen: `STEPHEN PRAYS FOR HIS KILLERS.` · `PERSECUTION, NAMED AHEAD OF TIME.` · `AS IF IN CHAINS WITH THEM.` · `QUIETER PRESSURE, AND NAMES SAID ALOUD.` · then, large: `BLESSED ARE THEY THAT SUFFER PERSECUTION.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold one community under pressure. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one place where believers practice at risk, from the news or from today's lesson. If you know a name, use it. If you don't, think of one parish, one family, getting dressed for Sunday knowing what it might cost them. Stay with them for a few slow breaths. In the same sermon, Jesus asks his listeners to pray for those who persecute them, too. If you pray, you can pray for both. If you don't, hold them all in mind with respect. The bell holds the time.
Martyr. The word for believers killed for their faith; Catholics under pressure today are the Church's newest witnesses, practicing at real risk.
Your line: not only long ago. Today, look up one Christian community under pressure right now, and say its name or its town out loud once. Day nine hundred forty-four.

howItsDone: Catholics pray for persecuted Christians in the prayers of the faithful at Mass, some parishes light their churches red on a day of remembrance, and charities support communities under pressure.

fork.setup: you're a bishop in a country where preaching freely could mean prison. what do you do?
options: keep preaching, and stay with your people.
fork.reveal: when the government put a group of prisoners on a flight out of the country, Bishop Rolando Álvarez refused to board. he was sentenced to prison, and later sent into exile.

what a scholar hears: some readers notice that Acts tells Stephen's death as an echo of Jesus's own, with a prayer for those who kill him.
